title: Abstract DP168: Chronic Stroke Plasma Triggers Microglial Activation and Cognitive Decline in Young Mice

evidence_spans.quote: Results: Mice infused with chronic stroke plasma exhibited impairments in recognition memory
aged (18-month-old) male and female C57Bl/6 mice
senescent-like phenotypes were confirmed using immunohistochemistry
Our ongoing work aims to identify the molecular mediators of these effects through multi-omic profiling.

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This empirical mouse study confirms senescent-like phenotypes, so cellular senescence is analyzed. Multi-omic profiling is described only as ongoing future work; no current-report molecular omics modality is stated.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: Retro-orbital infusion of plasma from aged mice in the chronic phase of ischemic stroke
causal_design_reviewer.comparator: Plasma from sham-surgery aged donor mice
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Recipient-mouse recognition and associative memory impairment and microglial activation
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Outcomes in young recipients infused with chronic-stroke plasma versus sham plasma
